title: Bayesian safety signal detection with bssd
text: study drug placebo randomized ratio \(k:1\). prior distribution placebo parameters based historical placebo data event rate \(\lambda_{HP}\) total patient time \(PT_{HP}\), discounted factor \(DF\). BDRIBS. number subjects event blinded data, \(Y\), follows \[Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}\{E \delta (r k + 1) / (k + 1)\},\] \(E\) exposure, \(\delta\) event rate placebo \(r\) rate ratio study drug placebo. priors \(\delta \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\lambda_{HP} PT_{HP} / DF, PT_{HP} / DF)\) shape rate parameters, \(r = p / \{k (1 - p)\}\) \(p \sim \mathrm{Beta}(, b)\). BDRIBS(1) uses total exposure time \(E\). BDRIBS(2) uses total time risk, leaves time first occurrence event. computed time_at_risk(). EXP_BERN. Subject \(\) follow-time \(t_i\) event (\(Y_i = 1\)) probability \[P(Y_i = 1) = w_p \{1 - \exp(-\lambda_p t_i)\} + w_d \{1 - \exp(-r \lambda_p t_i)\},\] \(w_p = 1 / (k + 1)\) \(w_d = k / (k + 1)\). priors \(\lambda_p\) \(r\) \(\delta\) \(r\) BDRIBS. LL_BERN. exponential distribution replaced log-logistic distribution, \[P(Y_i = 1) = w_p F(t_i; \mu_p, \sigma_p) + w_d F(t_i; \mu_d, \sigma_d), \quad F(t; \mu, \sigma) = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + \exp\{(\log t - \mu) / \sigma\}},\] hazard can change time (ll_cdf()). relative risk ratio cumulative incidences time \(t^*\), \(RR(t^*) = F(t^*; \mu_d, \sigma_d) / F(t^*; \mu_p, \sigma_p)\). Duncan (2026) state relative risk used model. ?llbern_post describes choice priors. signal declared posterior probability relative risk exceeds critical value \(rr_0\) larger threshold, \(P(RR > rr_0 \mid \mathrm{data}) > \mathrm{cutoff}\). defaults \(rr_0 = 1\) \(\mathrm{cutoff} = 0.95\).

title: Bayesian safety signal detection with bssd
text: Hypothetical example 2 Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018, Section 4.4) 2:1 randomization, background event rate 0.011 per patient-year placebo, 540 patient-years blinded exposure. screening analysis article treats background rate known, corresponds pt_hp = Inf. uniform prior \(p\), posterior probabilities 8 9 events published values computed MCMC bdribs package, differ values bssd 0.004. print method summarizes posterior 9 events: posterior mean \(r\) 1.52, article reports 1.53. article gives (0.52, 2.83) 95% interval \(r\). agrees equal-tailed 90% interval, (0.51, 2.82), level = 0.90 gives, equal-tailed 95% interval (0.38, 3.14).
code: ex2 <- expand.grid(rr0 = c(1, 1.3), y = c(8, 9)) ex2$bssd <- mapply(function(y, rr0) {   bdribs_post(y = y, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011, pt_hp = Inf,               p_prior = c(1, 1), rr0 = rr0, details = FALSE)$prob }, ex2$y, ex2$rr0) ex2$published <- c(0.622, 0.434, 0.756, 0.584) knitr::kable(ex2[, c("y", "rr0", "bssd", "published")], digits = 3,              col.names = c("Events", "rr0", "bssd", "Mukhopadhyay et al.")) fit9 <- bdribs_post(y = 9, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011,                     pt_hp = Inf, p_prior = c(1, 1)) fit9 #> Model: BDRIBS  #> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo #> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.753 #> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no #> Posterior of r: mean 1.522, median 1.438, 95% interval (0.379, 3.143) fit90 <- bdribs_post(y = 9, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011,                      pt_hp = Inf, p_prior = c(1, 1), level = 0.90)

code: set.seed(2026) d <- sim_blinded(n = 150, k = 1, accrual = 26, follow_up = 104,                  analysis_time = 117, dist = "loglogistic",                  par_p = c(7.3, 0.8), par_d = c(5.85, 0.8)) head(d[, c("id", "entry", "follow_up", "event", "event_time")]) #>   id     entry follow_up event event_time #> 1  1 14.446685  102.5533     0         NA #> 2  2  3.150173  104.0000     0         NA #> 3  3  3.683752  104.0000     0         NA #> 4  4  3.806313  104.0000     0         NA #> 5  5  9.020966  104.0000     0         NA #> 6  6  1.833814  104.0000     0         NA tar <- time_at_risk(d$follow_up, d$event, d$event_time) tar #>     exposure time_at_risk      n_event  #>     15096.61     14605.76        14.00 lambda_hp <- -log(1 - ll_cdf(104, mu = 7.3, sigma = 0.8)) / 104 pt_weeks <- 75 * 104 fits <- list(   BDRIBS1 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]], exposure = tar[["exposure"]],                         k = 1, lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks,                         df = 2, t_star = 104),   BDRIBS2 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]],                         exposure = tar[["time_at_risk"]], k = 1,                         lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2,                         t_star = 104),   EXP_BERN = expbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1,                           lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2,                           t_star = 104),   LL_BERN = llbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1, mu_hp = 7.3,                         sigma_hp = 0.8, pt_hp = pt_weeks / 52, df_p = 2,                         t_star = 104) ) res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, summary)) res$model <- names(fits) knitr::kable(res[, c("model", "prob", "signal", "rr_median", "ip_placebo",                      "ip_drug", "ip_difference")], digits = 3,              row.names = FALSE) sig <- res$model[res$signal]

title: Bayesian Safety Signal Detection for Blinded Clinical Trial Data
text: Hypothetical example 2 Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018, Section 4.4) 9 subjects event 540 patient-years blinded exposure, 2:1 randomization, known background rate 0.011 per patient-year placebo. posterior probability r > 1 0.753. article reports 0.756, computed MCMC bdribs package. four models applied simulated subject-level data (150 subjects, 1:1 randomization, log-logistic times event, analysis week 117): vignette("bssd") explains models, priors example simulation operating characteristics. documentation also available https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/.
code: library(bssd) fit <- bdribs_post(y = 9, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011,                    pt_hp = Inf, p_prior = c(1, 1)) fit #> Model: BDRIBS  #> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo #> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.753 #> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no #> Posterior of r: mean 1.522, median 1.438, 95% interval (0.379, 3.143) set.seed(2026) d <- sim_blinded(n = 150, k = 1, accrual = 26, follow_up = 104,                  analysis_time = 117, dist = "loglogistic",                  par_p = c(7.3, 0.8), par_d = c(5.85, 0.8)) tar <- time_at_risk(d$follow_up, d$event, d$event_time) lambda_hp <- -log(1 - ll_cdf(104, mu = 7.3, sigma = 0.8)) / 104 pt_weeks <- 75 * 104 fits <- list(   BDRIBS1 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]], exposure = tar[["exposure"]],                         k = 1, lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks,                         df = 2),   BDRIBS2 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]],                         exposure = tar[["time_at_risk"]], k = 1,                         lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2),   EXP_BERN = expbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1,                           lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2),   LL_BERN = llbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1, mu_hp = 7.3,                         sigma_hp = 0.8, pt_hp = pt_weeks / 52, df_p = 2,                         t_star = 104) ) res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, summary)) res$model <- names(fits) res[, c("model", "prob", "signal", "rr_median", "error")] #>             model      prob signal rr_median        error #> BDRIBS1   BDRIBS1 0.7909268  FALSE  2.879204           NA #> BDRIBS2   BDRIBS2 0.8049487  FALSE  3.030938           NA #> EXP_BERN EXP_BERN 0.8202780  FALSE  3.242503 1.814905e-07 #> LL_BERN   LL_BERN 0.9351465  FALSE  4.217216 3.733315e-04

text: subject \(\) follow-time \(t_i\), model $$P(Y_i = 1) = w_p [1 - \exp(-\lambda_p t_i)] + w_d [1 - \exp(-r \lambda_p t_i)],$$ \(w_p = 1 / (k + 1)\) \(w_d = k / (k + 1)\), $$\lambda_p \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\lambda_{HP} PT_{HP} / DF, PT_{HP} / DF), \quad r = p / [k (1 - p)], \quad p \sim \mathrm{Beta}(, b).$$ Gamma distribution parameterized shape rate. two-dimensional posterior integrated numerically coordinates \(\log \lambda_p\) prior distribution function \(p\). latter keeps tails posterior \(p\) control: likelihood vanish \(r \0\) \(r \\infty\), tails follow prior. coarse grid first locates region holds control$eps posterior mass marginal. region, Gauss-Legendre quadrature used \(\log \lambda_p\), marginal density second coordinate interpolated Chebyshev points, gives distribution function point (used prob quantiles \(r\)). control$check TRUE, computation repeated 1.5 times many nodes, finer result returned, absolute difference prob reported integration error estimate. likelihood stays positive \(r \\infty\), posterior means \(r\) \(r \lambda_p\) infinite second shape parameter Beta prior 1 less, default c(0.5, 0.5). returned Inf, posterior median \(r\) summary use. signal declared \(P(r > rr_0 \mid \mathrm{data}) > \) cutoff.

code: set.seed(1) n <- 60 t <- runif(n, 4, 104) y <- rbinom(n, 1, ll_cdf(t, mu = 6.5, sigma = 0.8)) fit <- llbern_post(y, t, k = 1, mu_hp = 6.5, sigma_hp = 0.8, pt_hp = 200,                    t_star = 104, control = list(check = FALSE)) fit #> Model: LL_BERN  #> Relative risk: ratio of cumulative incidences at t_star = 104  #> P(RR(t_star) > 1 | data) = 0.2741 #> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no #> Posterior of RR(t_star): mean 0.7703, median 0.1454, 95% interval (1.012e-119, 4.212) #> Cumulative incidence at t_star = 104: placebo 0.09706, study drug 0.06457, difference -0.03249

title: bssd 0.1.0
text: First version. bdribs_post() computes posterior distribution rate ratio BDRIBS model Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) specified Duncan (2026), total exposure time (BDRIBS(1)) total time risk (BDRIBS(2)) exposure. background rate Gamma prior historical placebo data (lambda_hp, pt_hp, df), known pt_hp = Inf (screening analysis Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018). expbern_post() llbern_post() compute posterior distributions exponential Bernoulli (EXP_BERN) log-logistic Bernoulli (LL_BERN) mixture models Duncan (2026) subject-level data (y, t). LL_BERN, relative risk ratio cumulative incidences t_star, priors study drug parameters can set mu_d_prior sigma_d_prior. posterior quantities computed numerical integration instead Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. expbern_post() llbern_post() repeat computation finer grid report estimate integration error control$check TRUE (default). time_at_risk() computes total exposure time total time risk subject-level data. ll_cdf() ll_mu() give cumulative incidence location parameter log-logistic distribution. sim_blinded() simulates blinded trial data exponential log-logistic times event, sim_oc() estimates operating characteristics models simulation. print() summary() methods results (class bssd_post). folder inst/reproduce reproduces numerical results Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) Duncan (2026), inst/validation compares package bdribs package, MCMC JAGS independent Python implementations.
